name: Question 3
problem: Use the first three non-zero terms of the Taylor expansion for $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)$ about $x=0$ to approximate the value of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1.5).$ Give your answer to $3$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
We use Taylor's formula in the form

$$
f(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{{f}^{″}(a)}{2!}(x-a)^{2}+⋯,
$$

with $a=0.$ 

Calculating the necessary derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1) \\ f(0) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(0+1)=0 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{x+1} \\ {f}^{′}(0) & =\frac{1}{0+1}=1 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-\frac{1}{(x+1)^{2}} \\ {f}^{″}(0) & =-\frac{1}{(0+1)^{2}}=-1 \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =\frac{2}{(x+1)^{3}} \\ {f}^{‴}(0) & =\frac{2}{(0+1)^{3}}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the Taylor series is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1) & =(0)+(1)(x-0)+\frac{(-1)}{2!}(x-0)^{2}+\frac{(2)}{3!}(x-0)^{3}+⋯ \\  & =x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute $x=0.5$ into the above to approximate $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1.5).$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡1.5 & ≈(0.5)-\frac{1}{2}(0.5)^{2}+\frac{1}{3}(0.5)^{3} \\  & =0.417\,,\end{aligned}
$$

to three decimal places.

html:
Question 3
?

Use the first three non-zero terms of the Taylor expansion for f(x)=ln⁡(x+1) about x=0 to approximate the value of ln⁡(1.5). Give your answer to 3 decimal places.

a
 ln⁡(1.5)≈0.424
b
 ln⁡(1.5)≈0.421
c
 ln⁡(1.5)≈0.415
d
 ln⁡(1.5)≈0.412
e
 ln⁡(1.5)≈0.417
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We use Taylor's formula in the form f(x)=f(a)+f′(a)(x−a)+f″(a)2!(x−a)2+⋯, with a=0.

Calculating the necessary derivatives, we get

f(x)=ln⁡(x+1)f(0)=ln⁡(0+1)=0f′(x)=1x+1f′(0)=10+1=1f″(x)=−1(x+1)2f″(0)=−1(0+1)2=−1f‴(x)=2(x+1)3f‴(0)=2(0+1)3=2.

So, the Taylor series is ln⁡(x+1)=(0)+(1)(x−0)+(−1)2!(x−0)2+(2)3!(x−0)3+⋯=x−12x2+13x3+⋯.

We substitute x=0.5 into the above to approximate ln⁡(1.5). We get

ln⁡1.5≈(0.5)−12(0.5)2+13(0.5)3=0.417, to three decimal places.
